themes_detail.label: Street noise spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 54 this week, a 304% increase from the 13.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.43), suggesting a sudden and acute disruption to neighborhood quiet.
evidence: 54 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 13.4 weekly average (304% spike, z-score: 8.43)
Highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating sudden neighborhood disruption
Timing suggests recent source or event triggering complaints
reporting_angles: What construction, commercial activity, or event triggered the sudden noise surge? Interview residents and local businesses.
Is there a specific location or time of day driving complaints? Map the 311 data to identify hotspots.

themes_detail.label: Garbage disposal complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped to 23 this week, a 318% increase from the 5.5-complaint weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.64), indicating either a service failure or a concentrated community frustration.
evidence: 23 residential disposal complaints this week vs. 5.5 weekly average (318% increase, z-score: 7.64)
Second-highest statistical anomaly, indicating coordinated or systemic issue
Timing overlaps with street sweeping complaint spike, suggesting possible sanitation system problem
reporting_angles: Is there a collection service disruption or missed pickups on specific blocks? Contact DSNY and residents.
Are residents dealing with overflowing bins or rodent activity tied to disposal issues? Investigate root cause.

themes_detail.label: Police calls jump 352%
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints spiked to 13 this week, a 352% increase from the 2.9-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.97), suggesting a sudden rise in criminal activity or community safety concerns.
evidence: 13 non-emergency police complaints this week vs. 2.9 weekly average (352% increase, z-score: 6.97)
Third-highest spike by z-score, indicating statistically significant anomaly
Convergence with noise spike suggests possible public disorder or disturbance events
reporting_angles: What types of non-emergency incidents are driving the spike? Request NYPD complaint data and precinct logs.
Are residents reporting street crime, quality-of-life violations, or disturbances? Interview community members and local leaders.

themes_detail.label: Street sweeping neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 16 last week, a 753% increase from the 1.9-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.41), indicating possible sanitation crew failures or reduced street maintenance coverage.
evidence: 16 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 1.9 weekly average (753% spike, z-score: 6.41)
Largest proportional increase in dataset, indicating severe departure from normal
Overlaps with garbage disposal spike and dirty condition complaints, suggesting broader sanitation breakdown
reporting_angles: Are DSNY crews being reassigned or understaffed? Check scheduling, staffing levels, and maintenance routes.
Which blocks or neighborhoods are being neglected? Field reporting to document uncleaned streets and debris.

themes_detail.label: Traffic signal failures
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints spiked to 133 two weeks ago, a 297% increase from the 33.5-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.91), indicating possible infrastructure breakdown affecting traffic flow and pedestrian safety.
evidence: 133 traffic signal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 33.5 weekly average (297% increase, z-score: 5.91)
Single-week spike suggests acute failure event rather than gradual degradation
Potential public safety impact given traffic signal role in pedestrian and vehicular safety
reporting_angles: What caused the widespread signal failures? Contact DOT to investigate outages and repair timeline.
Which major intersections were affected? Document traffic congestion and safety incidents during the spike period.
